policy.status: Alternative-history planning forecast, not observed market data or negotiated price schedule
policy.geography: Worldwide microcomputer unit shipments; Logix includes UK distributor shipments. Five clone brands counted only for their compatible product lines. Other legacy products of those brands remain in other manufacturers.
demand_basis: Author assumption: foresight aligns production and purchased components with finite customer demand. No factory bottleneck or lost sales; no infinite demand, automatic sell-through of arbitrary production, or zero capital costs.

Budget colour and 5 MB configurations enter in May 1980. Native application value, two drives and complete-package pricing improve new-business conversion; IBM has a March 1982 substitute-OS launch, not the historical DOS ecosystem.

Gross factors are explicit low-confidence scenario judgements relative to the frozen same-quarter 1980/81/82 baseline, not measured price elasticities. 1983 uses original 1982 quarters. No historical Apple/IBM dominance is imposed.

Budget purchases substitute for existing Artemis configurations inside the family total; 10/15 percentage points of 1981/82 Logix mix shift from Aurelia+ to Artemis. Clone cannibalisation is deducted once.
Demand scenarios remain finite; capacity follows each scenario. Actual support and supplier qualification are assumed funded, not free. 1983 holds 1982 pricing/costs.

capacity.basis: Adam foresees volumes. Incremental capacity is funded one quarter before use, with 5% headroom; no production cap clips sales. Engineering cost allowance, not a released equipment plan.

market.basis: 1981/1982 contemporaneous Dataquest estimates reported by TIME; scope comparability is approximate. 1983 round planning assumption, not a sourced historical count. business_market.definition: Disk-equipped computers bought for business use, worldwide; exclude home/education purchases even if disk-equipped. All modelled Logix/clone systems allocated to business for this segment estimate.
business_market.basis: Illustrative addressable-market assumptions, not observed counts. All-vendor retail datasets do not establish business-use classification. 20% of platform volume expands baseline; remainder displaces competitors. Rival weights distribute only residual business demand.

financial_policy.scope: Logix computer task bundles only. Additional paid offers and clone supply/royalties are separate streams in ROI. Autodesk licence receipts excluded from project revenue.
financial_policy.retail_spend: Quantity × dated retail_price_usd for every weighted basket offer.
financial_policy.after_channel_fees: Quantity × dated revenue_after_fee_usd, already net of the modeled fee.
financial_policy.recurring_cost: Quantity × dated manufacturing_cost_usd; includes the recurring contents and services defined in retail pricing.
financial_policy.contribution: After channel fees minus recurring cost, before corporate development, marketing, capital/depreciation and tax.
financial_policy.timing: Use dated June/December catalogue assessments; June snapshots proxy whole June, COMDEX CAD shipments begin December 1982. 1983 holds December 1982 unit prices/costs; new Office Professional and Business Accounts priced contents replace legacy variants. Pending installation/backup scope is not claimed as a firm quote; support/qualification allowances remain explicit. No speculative process savings.
financial_policy.rounding: Round each weighted offer line to cents, then sum lines, months, quarters and years. Contribution is net receipts minus recurring cost in integer cents.
financial_policy.demand: 1980–83 reassessment; clone cannibalisation and CAD substitution explicit.
